title: Inaccessibility of the Cosmological Singularity to Quantum Probes
authors: Vishnulal Cheriyodathillathu, Saurya Das, Soumen Basak, Tanmay Patil
abstract: We propose an operational resolution of the FLRW big bang singularity using quantum probes satisfying a curvature coupled Klein-Gordon equation. Applying the Madelung-Bohm decomposition of a Klein-Gordon field on a classical near-singularity FLRW background, we show that the induced conformal geometry renders curvature invariants finite and makes past directed causal geodesics complete. The classical big bang surface is therefore inaccessible to this class of quantum probes in finite effective proper time, while the underlying FLRW spacetime remains singular.
summary: This work addresses the Big Bang singularity by treating quantum probes governed by a Klein-Gordon equation on an FLRW background. By analyzing the effective geometry experienced by the probe, the authors show that while the classical spacetime remains singular, the quantum probe cannot reach the singularity in any finite effective time. This suggests an operational resolution of the singularity.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the classical Big Bang singularity in cosmology is physically accessible to quantum probes.
main_result: The classical singularity is operationally inaccessible to quantum probes because the effective geometry experienced by the probe renders curvature invariants finite and requires infinite effective proper time to reach the singularity.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of a quantum scalar field (Klein-Gordon probe) on a classical FLRW background using the Madelung-Bohm decomposition and examining the resulting conformally related effective metric.
model_or_system: The system is the FLRW spacetime background, and the probe is modeled as a quantum scalar field $\Phi$ satisfying a curvature-coupled Klein-Gordon equation. The analysis focuses on the asymptotic behavior near $t 	o 0^+$.
key_observables: Curvature invariants (Ricci and Kretschmann scalars) in the effective geometry, and the proper time/affine parameter required to reach the singularity.
important_parameters: The coupling constants ($\xi, \eta$), the mass term ($m$), and the time evolution parameters derived from the asymptotic ansatz ($\Omega^2 \propto t^{-n}$).
main_assumptions: The probe does not backreact on the geometry (fixed classical background), and the analysis is restricted to homogeneous probe states.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the quantum probe dynamics via the coupled Klein-Gordon equation, applies the Madelung-Bohm decomposition, analyzes the asymptotic behavior near the singularity using power-law ansatzes, and concludes by comparing the finite effective proper time to the infinite required time.
why_interesting: The concept of operational resolution of singularities via quantum field theory in curved spacetime is a fundamental theoretical tool, drawing parallels to how quantum effects regularize classical infinities in other physical contexts.
